title: Why Functions and Modules Matter
learningObjectives: Explain how functions name and package reusable behavior.
Describe how modules organize related responsibilities.
Recognize how reuse reduces duplication and inconsistent updates.
Identify inputs, outputs, and side effects at component boundaries.
Choose abstractions that improve clarity without unnecessary complexity.

understand.concept: A function packages instructions under a meaningful name so a program can invoke that behavior when needed. A module groups related functions, data, or other code behind an organizing boundary. Functions support reuse of a behavior; modules help organize related behaviors. They are useful when they reduce repetition, clarify intent, or provide a testable boundary.
understand.whyItMatters: Repeated code can drift as fixes are applied unevenly. Named functions and purposeful modules make code easier to read, test, reuse, and maintain. However, unnecessary abstractions can make a simple program harder to follow, so the goal is clarity rather than maximizing the number of functions.
understand.analogy: A function is like a labeled task card: its name tells you what operation is available, and calling it asks the program to perform it.
understand.analogyLimit: Program functions may accept inputs, return values, or have side effects; the analogy does not capture all runtime behavior.

explain.narrative: A function definition establishes a named block of behavior. A call invokes that behavior, and in a typical synchronous flow control returns to the statement after the call. Naming should describe purpose from the caller's perspective. Functions can be reused with different data. Function and module syntax, visibility, and declaration-order rules vary by language.

examples.title: Reusable calculation
examples.code:
function area(width, height) { return width * height; }
console.log(area(4, 3));
examples.explanation: The named calculation can be reused for different dimensions.

examples.title: Reuse a decision rule
examples.explanation: A single rule centralizes the threshold and can be called with different values.

examples.title: Format a label
examples.code:
function label(name, count) { return name + ': ' + count; }
console.log(label('Books', 3));
examples.explanation: Formatting is separated from the caller's other work.

examples.title: Group related operations
examples.explanation: Related operations could be grouped in an inventory module with a clear purpose.

examples.title: Avoid duplicated logic
examples.explanation: One implementation is reused, avoiding divergent copies of a calculation.

commonMistakes: Expecting a definition to execute automatically.
Using vague names that hide purpose.
Copying logic rather than reusing a well-named function.
Assuming every function returns a value.
Ignoring language-specific declaration or visibility rules.

guidedTask.title: Guided practice: extract a shipping-cost rule
guidedTask.instructions: Create a function with a clear name, call it at least twice, predict output before running, and explain how reuse improves clarity.
steps: Give the function a purpose-revealing name.
Call it with two different scenarios where appropriate.
Explain where execution continues after a call.
guidedTask.starterCode: // Define a clearly named function here, then call it twice.

independentTask.title: Independent practice: reusable workflow
independentTask.instructions: Create a small program with three or four named functions for a simple workflow.
requirements: Each function has one clear responsibility.
Call functions in a deliberate order.
Write a short trace of the execution order.

hints: Definitions establish behavior; calls invoke it.
Use parameters for varying inputs rather than duplicating code.
Avoid needless abstraction for one-off trivial code.

questions.prompt: Why extract a repeated rule into a function?
questions.explanation: Centralizing logic makes changes less error-prone and supports reuse.

questions.prompt: What is a module commonly used for?
options: Grouping related code and exposing an interface
questions.answer: Grouping related code and exposing an interface
questions.explanation: Modules organize related responsibilities and define boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which function name communicates intent best?
questions.explanation: A meaningful name makes the call understandable without inspecting its body.

questions.prompt: When may a function abstraction be unnecessary?
options: When a one-off expression is clearer inline
questions.answer: When a one-off expression is clearer inline
questions.explanation: Abstractions should improve clarity, not add ceremony.

questions.prompt: What risk comes from duplicated business logic?
options: Copies can drift and be changed inconsistently
It always makes a program faster
questions.answer: Copies can drift and be changed inconsistently
questions.explanation: Duplicated rules may diverge when only some copies are updated.
